title: Probabilistic spot-cap controller and GPU-fractional routing for cost-stable inference
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a probabilistic routing controller that enforces per-customer rolling spend caps while maximizing use of cheaper spot capacity and preserving latency SLOs. The controller will use short-horizon spot-availability models per region/SKU, continuous GPU-class fractional routing (e.g., mix of A100/RTX/Trn types) and soft+hard budget caps with configurable degradation behavior (graceful throttling, model variant fallback, on-demand backfill). This ticket covers design, simulation, implementation of routing decision service, integration with existing smart routing policy layer, and runtime telemetry for cost/e2e latency tradeoff analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Controller exposes per-customer rolling spend cap config and enforces it across hosted + dedicated routing paths
Routing decisions include a probabilistic use-of-spot score and selected GPU-class fraction that maximizes expected cost savings while meeting 95th percentile latency SLOs

Fallback chain: prefer cheaper spot on matched SKUs -> mix with reserve on-demand fraction when risk > threshold -> fallback to compatible smaller model variant when spend cap hit or latency impossible
Simulated workloads with historical spot traces show >=12% cost reduction vs current deterministic fallback while keeping P95 latency < target for 90% of customers
End-to-end metrics surfaced in Console: per-customer cost burn, spot-usage fraction, eviction-risk, and routing decisions for last 7 days
Automated tests cover decision logic, policy config edge cases, and integration tests with scheduler mock
tasks: Design: define probabilistic model inputs (region, SKU, recent eviction rate, time-of-day, queue length)
Sim: implement Monte Carlo spot availability simulator using 18 months of provider traces
API: extend routing policy schema to include 'prob_spot_use' and 'gpu_fraction_map'
Runtime: implement router plugin that computes expected cost+latency utility and returns route plan
Telemetry: add events for routing decisions, expected vs realized cost, eviction events
E2E: run canary with 5 internal customers, monitor cost and latency for two weeks
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Chose probabilistic short-horizon model over deterministic thresholds; reason: preserves capacity while reducing false-positive shift to on-demand
2026-03-12: GPU-fractional routing chosen (fractional split to multiple GPU classes) instead of strict SKU priority; reason: allows gradual degradation and better packing
2026-03-12: Soft cap behavior will start by applying per-customer 'grace throttle' with token-bucket diminution before hard cap blocks; reason: prevents sudden user-facing errors
progress_updates: 2026-03-11: Initial design doc drafted and shared with PM and runtime leads (link in design_docs)
2026-03-12: Simulation harness scaffolded; imported spot eviction traces and verified distribution shaping
2026-03-13: Router plugin prototype implemented; unit tests for cost-utility passed locally
2026-03-13: Scheduled design review with infra and console teams for 2026-03-15
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Spot prediction errors could cause oscillations between spot and on-demand, increasing cost. Mitigation: damped update to spot probability and minimum sticky window (5 minutes) before rebalancing
Risk: Per-customer hard caps might cause sudden traffic drops for high-volume customers. Mitigation: soft cap stage with throttles and pre-notifications + optional grace top-up parameter
Risk: Mixing GPUs may complicate KV cache reuse and model performance. Mitigation: limit fractional routing to compatible model families and prefer warm-pool pre-warmed instances for small fractions
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal canary—routing decisions returned as 'suggested' and not enforced for 3 internal apps (2 weeks)
Phase 1: enable enforcement for internal teams and low-risk customers with conservative cap defaults (4 weeks)
Phase 2: gradual rollout to <10% of production customers with telemetry gates for cost and latency
Phase 3: full rollout after 8 weeks of stable metrics and postmortem
notes: Related: tie into Optimize's recommendations so customers can opt into recommended gpu_fraction_map and cap thresholds
Follow-up: UI work in Console to let customers visualize spot-eviction risk and set reactive behaviors (notify, degrade, block)
